name: tv-power-off
title: TV Power Off
description: Ends a scene like a switched-off tube: the picture squashes into a bright horizontal line, the line pinches to a phosphor dot, the dot fades and the frame is dead black. Runs its WebGL shader over its own built-in scene (a render queue list; title, rows and background from variables), not over the host video. Plays once: 25 frames of picture, an 18-frame collapse, then black.
useWhen: A scene should end like a device being switched off rather than fading out.
The video is about something that lives on a screen (a terminal, a dashboard, a retro build) and powering it down is the punctuation.
A beat needs a hard end: everything after the collapse is black.
avoidWhen: The tube look should hold for the whole scene instead of ending it: use crt-screen.
Both scenes should be visible while the change happens: reach for a transition such as glitch-cut.
The frame has to stay transparent once the scene is gone: what this leaves behind is opaque black.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Title
variables.description: Small heading above the list in the sample scene.

variables.label: Rows
variables.description: Rows of the list as name | status, separated by semicolons (up to 5).
variables.default: intro-scene.mp4 | Done; feature-tour.mp4 | Rendering; pricing-outro.mp4 | Queued

variables.label: Delay
variables.description: Frames of untouched picture before the power-off starts (30 per second).

variables.label: Gain
variables.description: How much the squashed picture brightens as it collapses.

variables.label: Afterglow
variables.description: Size of the glowing line and dot.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. The collapsed line is a pixel thin at the end; lower renders faster but softens it.
